propositions: The undecomposed hard-override axis fires on 0.107–0.153% of findings (11/10,250 to 18/11,773), two orders of magnitude below other severity axes, yet its non-none grades floor impact at 0.85 regardless of grade level (low equals high).

The axis justification cites a deterministic G5 suppressor to explain low fire rate, but that suppressor never fired in 2,000 recorded reviews and is inapplicable to 90%+ of reviewed tickets which are childless.

The inverse population (findings text-matched to the undecomposed regex but graded none) consists of 33–50 regex false positives in code-decomposition findings rather than missed flat-plan defects, negating the hypothesis of a large dark class.

At least 25 of 29 fires had undecomposed as the sole hard-override criterion, and 16 of 29 were graded low; one low-grade fire alone blocked a plan via the 0.85 floor, demonstrating miscalibration identical to the divergent_implementation and ac_unverifiable axes before their retunes.

The axis hedge citing the inert suppressor must be rewritten, and the grade-to-floor mapping must be gated on medium|high grades or converted to a closed kind set to prevent low grades from producing hard blocks.
